'''Jen-Chieh Peng''' ({{lang-zh |c = 彭仁傑}}; born 1949) is a Taiwanese-American experimental nuclear physicist at the [[University of Illinois Urbana–Champaign]].<ref name="profile">{{cite web |title=Jen-Chieh Peng |url=https://physics.illinois.edu/people/directory/profile/jcpeng |website=physics.illinois.edu |access-date=13 September 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Peng earned his bachelor's degree in physics from [[Tunghai University]] in [[Taiwan]] in 1970 and his Ph.D. in nuclear physics from the [[University of Pittsburgh]] in 1975. He worked as a researcher at the [[Saclay Nuclear Research Centre|Centre d'Études Nucléaires de Saclay]] in France before joining the Physics Division of [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]] in 1978. Peng joined the faculty at Illinois Physics in 2002 as a full professor.<ref>{{cite news |title=Jen-Chieh Peng |url=https://academicians.sinica.edu.tw/index.php?r=academician-n%2Fshow&id=771 |access-date=19 February 2023 |publisher=Academia Sinica}}</ref>

Peng's areas of research include [[Parton (particle physics)|partonic structures]] of hadrons, fundamental symmetries, and neutrino physics. He is a spokesperson or co-spokesperson of some 10 nuclear and particle physics experiments and a coauthor of over 430 journal articles, cited more than 50,000 times.

Peng was elected a Fellow of the American Physical Society in 1993 and a Laboratory Fellow at the Los Alamos National Laboratory in 1997. In 2022 he was elected an Academician of the Academia Sinica.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |title=Newly Elected Academicians Announced for Academia Sinica's 33rd Academicians Election— 19 New Academicians and 3 Honorary Academicians Elected |url=https://www.sinica.edu.tw/en/news/7238 |access-date=13 September 2022 |website=Academia Sinica}}</ref> In 2022 he received the Tom W. Bonner Prize in Nuclear Physics<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Prize Recipient |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Peng&first_nm=Jen-Chieh&year=2023 |access-date=2022-10-17 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref> with the citation "for pioneering work on studying antiquark distributions in the nucleons and nuclei using the Drell-Yan process as an experimental tool, and for seminal work on elucidating the origins of the flavor asymmetries of light-quark sea in the nucleons".
